Any single-mode f would force −iω as an eigenvalue, excluded by det(A+iωI)=−irω, so the mode with strictly larger real part cannot cancel. At matched rates above the critical gap the modulus after removing e^(−rt) is strictly positive and periodic (its imaginary sine term and real cosine cannot vanish together); at equality it is the modulus of a nonvanishing linear polynomial times the exponential. These give the full log limit, not merely an envelope. The positive quadratic γ|f|²+r|h|² has derivative −2rγ|f−h|², and f=h is not an eigenline for ω≠0, giving strict spectral stability. For γ<r the trace bound is strict; for d=γ−r>0, |Δ|²−(2d²−Re Δ)²=16rγd²>0 forces Re √Δ>d. At γ=r the bound is saturated exactly for |ω|≥2r. At the critical gap the nonzero off-diagonal of the repeated-root matrix guarantees a nontrivial Jordan block and the initial state gives a nonzero linear term in the observed coherence. Direct differentiation yields the stated nonpositive derivative, with only isolated zeros in the oscillatory regime and the negative critical limit for t>0. All matched-rate f are nonzero for finite times, so f(t)/f(s) defines a CPTP dephasing map; trace-distance monotonicity follows also by shrinking transverse differences while leaving diagonal differences fixed.
